facts.text: The rufous whistler makes up for its subdued reddish-brown and grey plumage with its remarkable song-making ability.
facts.quote: Predominantly a reddish-brown and grey bird, it makes up for its subdued plumage with its song-making ability.

facts.text: Male rufous whistlers have rufous underparts, a dark-grey back, white throat and often a black mask over the head.
facts.quote: males have rufous underparts and predominantly dark-grey back and tail with white throats and (in most cases) a black mask that covers most of their head and some of their neck.

facts.text: Its long tail is almost as long as the rest of the bird, very narrow, with a sharp forked tip.
facts.quote: They have short beaks and long tails (almost as long as the rest of the bird) which are very narrow and have sharp, forked tips.

facts.text: The rufous whistler's musical calls consist of a lengthy series of ringing notes.
facts.quote: The rufous whistler has a variety of musical calls which consist of a lengthy series of ringing notes.

facts.text: Both parents incubate the eggs and care for the young, with incubation lasting about 13 days on average.
facts.quote: Breeding in monogamous pairs, both males and females incubate their eggs and care for their young. The period of incubation is about 13 days on average.

facts.text: The female alone builds a cup-shaped nest, gluing it to a branch with strands of spider web.
facts.quote: The female alone constructs the nest, which usually consists of a combination of twigs, vines, grass and other matter formed in a cup-like shape and attached to a tree branch using strands from spider webs.

facts.text: Rufous whistlers mainly eat insects but also take seeds, fruit and occasionally leaves and grasses.
facts.quote: While rufous whistlers primarily feed on insects, they also eat seeds, fruit and occasionally, leaves and grasses.

facts.text: Unusually for a whistler, the rufous whistler never forages for food on the ground.
facts.quote: They never forage for food on the ground which is unusual for whistlers which typically do not forage at particularly high levels.

facts.text: It migrates seasonally, moving south in spring and north in autumn.
facts.quote: It migrates seasonally, moving south in the spring and north in the autumn.

facts.text: The Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay people of northern New South Wales call this bird mulindjal or mulimuli.
facts.quote: The Gamilaraay and Yuwaalaraay people of northern New South Wales use the names mulindjal or mulimuli to refer to this species.
